1	---
     2	name: ui-layout
     3	description: Use for Layout Tree decisions involving Row, Column, Stack, Panel, Slot, Sidebar, dimensions, resizing, placement, and composition of existing plugin nodes.
     4	compatibility: Agent UI Plugin Creator AppUIModel and deterministic compiler boundary.
     5	allowed-tools: enable_creator_tools read_file ls glob grep inspect_ui_project inspect_app_ui_model inspect_ui_slots list_ui_plugins inspect_ui_plugin mutate_app_ui_model execute
     6	---
     7	
     8	# UI Layout
     9	
    10	Express composition through the AppUIModel Layout Tree rather than DOM manipulation or ad-hoc Plugin CSS.
    11	
    12	Do not load this Skill for an eligible `insert_plugin_default` request from a
    13	fresh Composition Snapshot. The Host resolves the declared authoring placement,
    14	size, track materialization, and low-level lowering atomically. Load this Skill
    15	when the semantic operation is unavailable, fails closed, or the user requests
    16	custom Layout placement or geometry.
    17	
    18	## Node semantics
    19	
    20	- `sidebar`: wraps the main `content` and ordered single-plugin navigation `items`.
    21	- `row`: lays out children horizontally. Optional `sizes` correspond by index to `children`.
    22	- `column`: lays out children vertically. Optional `sizes` correspond by index to `children`.
    23	- `stack`: overlays or switches among children; `activeIndex` selects a direct child by index.
    24	- `panel`: wraps one child and may define width, height, min/max width, or resizing.
    25	- `slot`: is a physical structural location with an ordered `plugins` array. It has no persisted id, description, hint, or Runtime slot id.
    26	
    27	## Layout rules
    28	
    29	- Preserve existing child order and regions unless the request says otherwise.
    30	- Use the observed `nodeRef` only for the current mutation snapshot. Store each visual plugin directly in the Slot where it appears.
    31	- For a fixed right region, use a Row with the main content first and a right Panel second.
    32	- When a Row `sizes` entry and a child Panel `width` describe the same fixed dimension, update both consistently.
    33	- For Row and Column layouts, the parent `sizes` owns the grid tracks. A fixed-size child Panel does not shrink its parent track. For a fixed sidebar, set the parent tracks to `[W, minmax(0, 1fr)]` and use the matching child Panel width when that authoring constraint is also needed. `gap` only controls space between tracks; inspect the parent tracks and child bounds before attributing a visible layout issue to `gap`.
    34	- Creator Row/Column track sizes always use explicit CSS strings. Correct values
    35	  include `"280px"`, `"1fr"`, and `"minmax(0, 1fr)"`; never send numeric
    36	  track sizes through Creator mutation operations. Runtime numeric Row/Column
    37	  sizes represent fractional tracks, not pixels. A fixed sidebar example is
    38	  `["280px", "minmax(0, 1fr)"]`.
    39	- When inserting into a Row or Column that already has `sizes`, pass the new
    40	  child's `size` on `insert_layout_node`, `move_layout_node`, or
    41	  `insert_layout_relative`; a later `update_layout_node_props` cannot rescue an
    42	  earlier sequential operation that already failed. When
    43	  `insert_layout_relative` creates a new sized wrapper, pass `size` and
    44	  `anchorSize` together.
    45	- Use a nested Column for vertical subdivision and Stack only when overlapping or active-view behavior is intended.
    46	- Do not add a plugin node until you have confirmed the referenced Plugin exists.
    47	- Do not edit Runtime layout code for an application-specific arrangement.
    48	
    49	For a pure Layout change, start from
    50	`inspect_ui_project({"view":"composition"})`; do not re-read AppUIModel,
    51	manifests, Plugin source, CSS, Services, or generated files when that fresh
    52	snapshot already contains the needed refs, sizes, Slots, instances, capability
    53	summaries, authoring placement/size guidance, Service readiness, Ho…
